core_obligations: Reduce the first and third assertions to the second, using that a closed subset with quasi-compact complement, and also a closed subset in a Noetherian scheme, is cut out by a finitely generated ideal, and that completions of Noetherian rings are Noetherian (proof lines 3289-3296).

Prove the second assertion: for a morphism from an affine scheme whose image lies in T, each of the chosen generators becomes nilpotent after pullback, hence some power of the ideal maps to zero (proof lines 3298-3303).
Conclude that the completion functor is the filtered colimit of the spectra of the quotients by the powers of the ideal, that is the formal spectrum of the adic completion (proof lines 3303-3306).
proof_roadmap: Reduction to the second assertion (proof lines 3289-3296).
Nilpotence of the pulled back generators (proof lines 3298-3303).
Identification with the formal spectrum of the completion (proof lines 3303-3306).
difficulty_reason: For an affine scheme X with a closed subset T, the lemma asserts three things about the formal completion of X along T: that it is adic* when the complement of T is quasi-compact, that it is the formal spectrum of the adic completion with respect to a finitely generated ideal cutting out T, and that it is Noetherian when X is (statement lines 3275-3287). The proof reduces the first two assertions to the second: if either the complement is quasi-compact or the scheme is Noetherian, then T is cut out by a finitely generated ideal, and in the Noetherian case the adic completion of a Noetherian ring is Noetherian, so it suffices to identify the completion in the case of an ideal cut out by finitely many elements (proof lines 3289-3296). That identification is a direct computation: a morphism from an affine scheme into X whose image lies in T has each of the chosen generators nilpotent after pullback, so some power of the ideal maps to zero, which says exactly that the functor is the filtered colimit of the spectra of the quotients by the powers of the ideal, that is the formal spectrum of the adic completion (proof lines 3298-3306). The claim is H2: the reduction of the two other assertions to the second uses the finite generation criterion in one case and permanence of Noetherianness under completion in the other, and the explicit identification of the functor is carried out.
